These dates are cut-off periods, and some programmes have earlier programme-specific deadlines (for example the portfolio for the Communication Design qualification test).

question: Are cooperative programmes "individual" degree programmes?
answer: No. The General Examination Regulations (APO) call them "cooperative programme variants" of regular degree programmes. Cooperative students mostly take the same courses as regular students. They choose specialisation modules with the practice partner and complete the internship semester and final thesis with the partner.

audience: Students and applicants in cooperative study programmes
question: How can I become a cooperative student?
answer: Find an offer on the Studienplatzportal (German only) and apply to both the practice partner and THWS. Apply to the practice partner well before applying to THWS. Timing depends on the variant: academic study with vocational training starts about one year before studies, and intensive in-company training starts in August or September. You sign a practice partner agreement and submit it at enrolment. Late placements may be possible in consultation with the programme director, the cooperative study coordinator, and the Department of Student Affairs.

question: How many sections does an exam consist of?
answer: Four sections, each worth 25% of the grade. The written exam covers Listening Comprehension, Reading Comprehension, and Written Production and Interaction. You must pass all four parts for a language certificate.

question: How can I obtain a DAAD language certificate?
answer: Requirements for study-abroad applications vary, so check early. THWS students who need English proof for study or internships abroad can email the Campus for Language Proficiency (CLP – Campus Sprache) to apply. The DAAD certificate requires a graded proof of a passed exam. If the proof is external (e.g., TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge FCE, Cambridge CAE), the CLP first decides whether to recognize it. Without graded proof, you can take a mobility test. It has two parts, in this order: 1. Online placement test "onSET-English": up to 40 minutes, supervised in Würzburg or Schweinfurt. 2. Oral test: 10–15 minutes, conducted by an authorized CLP examiner. The mobility test and certificate are free for THWS students. Mobility tests usually take place twice a year, in November and June. Contact the CLP by mail for exact dates.
